'''Julian Sahasrabudhe''' (born May 8, 1988) is a Canadian [[mathematician]] who is an [[assistant professor]] of mathematics at the [[University of Cambridge]], in their [[Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Sahasrabudhe |first=Julian |title=Personal homepage |url=https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/~jdrs2/ |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics |publisher=[[University of Cambridge]]}}</ref> His research interests are in [[Extremal combinatorics|extremal]] and [[probabilistic combinatorics]], [[Ramsey theory]], random polynomials and matrices, and [[combinatorial number theory]].

== Life and education ==
Sahasrabudhe grew up on [[Bowen Island]], [[British Columbia]], Canada. He studied music at [[Capilano University|Capilano College]] and later moved to study at [[Simon Fraser University]] where he completed his undergraduate degree in mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 14, 2023 |title=Alum Julian Sahasrabudhe Featured in Quanta Magazine for Work on Ramsey Theory |url=https://www.sfu.ca/math/news/2023-news/SahasrabudheRamseyTheory.html |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=Department of Mathematics |publisher=[[Simon Fraser University]] |language=en}}</ref> After graduating in 2012, Julian received his Ph.D. in 2017 under the supervision of [[Béla Bollobás]] at the [[University of Memphis]].<ref name=":0" /> 

Following his Ph.D., Sahasrabudhe was a Junior Research Fellow at [[Peterhouse, Cambridge]] from 2017 to 2021.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |editor-last=Jungić |editor-first=Veselin|editor-link=Veselin Jungić |title=Julian Sahasrabudhe |url=https://www.sfu.ca/~vjungic/RamseyProjects/ssec_Julian.html |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=Introduction to Ramsey Theory: Students' Projects |publisher=[[Simon Fraser University]]}}</ref> He currently holds a position as an assistant professor in the Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics (DPMMS) at the University of Cambridge.<ref name=":0" /> 

== Career and research ==
Sahasrabudhe's work covers many topics such as Littlewood problems on polynomials, probability and geometry of polynomials, arithmetic Ramsey theory, Erdős covering systems, random matrices and polynomials, etc.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> In one of his more recent works in [[Ramsey theory]], he published a paper on ''Exponential Patterns in Arithmetic Ramsey Theory'' in 2018 by building on an observation made by Alessandro Sisto<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alessandro Sisto |url=https://scholar.google.ch/citations?user=_bTlVaMAAAAJ&hl=en |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=scholar.google.ch}}</ref> in 2011.<ref name="julian">{{cite journal |last=Sahasrabudhe |first=Julian |year=2018 |title=Exponential Patterns in Arithmetic Ramsey Theory |journal=Acta Arith. |volume=182 |pages=13–42 |doi=10.4064/aa8603-9-2017 |arxiv=1607.08396 }}</ref> He proved that for every finite colouring of the [[Natural number|natural numbers]] there exists <math> a, b > 1 </math> such that the triple <math> a,b,a^b </math> is monochromatic, demonstrating the partition regularity of complex exponential patterns. This work marks a crucial development in understanding the structure of numbers under partitioning.

In 2023, Sahasrabudhe submitted a paper titled ''An exponential improvement for diagonal Ramsey'' along with Marcelo Campos,<ref name=":3" /> Simon Griffiths,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Simon Griffiths |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=155306 |access-date=2024-03-15 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> and [[Robert Morris (mathematician)|Robert Morris]]. In this paper, they proved that the [[Ramsey's theorem|Ramsey number]] 

{{Center|<math> R(k) \leq (4-\epsilon)^k </math> for some constant <math> \epsilon > 0 </math>}} 

This is the first exponential improvement over the upper bound of [[Paul Erdős|Erdős]] and [[George Szekeres|Szekeres]], proved in 1935.<ref name="julian6">{{cite journal |last1=Sahasrabudhe |first1=Julian |last2=Campos |first2=Marcelo |last3=Griffiths |first3=Simon |last4=Morris |first4=Robert |year=2023 |title=An exponential improvement for diagonal Ramsey |journal=Submitted |arxiv=2303.09521 }}</ref>

Sahasrabudhe has also worked with Marcelo Campos,<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Marcelo Campos |url=https://marceloscampos.github.io/ |access-date=2024-03-11 |website=marceloscampos.github.io}}</ref> Matthew Jenssen,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Matthew Jenssen |url=http://matthewjenssen.com/ |access-date=2024-03-11 |website=matthewjenssen.com}}</ref> and Marcus Michelen<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marcus Michelen's Homepage |url=https://marcusmichelen.org/ |access-date=2024-03-11 |website=marcusmichelen.org}}</ref> on [[Random matrix|random matrix theory]] with the paper ''The singularity probability of a random symmetric matrix is exponentially small''.<ref name="julian5">{{cite journal |last1=Sahasrabudhe |first1=Julian |last2=Campos |first2=Marcelo |last3=Jenssen |first3=Matthew |last4=Michelen |first4=Marcus |title= The singularity probability of a random symmetric matrix is exponentially small|journal= Journal of the American Mathematical Society|date=2024 |volume=38 |pages=179–224 |arxiv=2105.11384 |doi=10.1090/jams/1042}}</ref> The paper addresses a long-standing conjecture concerning symmetric matrix with entries in <math> \{-1, 1\} </math>. They proved that the probability of such a matrix being [[Invertible matrix|singular]] is exponentially small. The research quantifies this probability as <math>\mathbb{P}(\det(A)=0)\leq e^{-cn} </math> where <math> A </math> is drawn uniformly at random from the set of all <math> n \times n </math> symmetric matrices and <math> c </math> is an absolute constant.

In 2020, Sahasrabudhe published a paper named ''Flat Littlewood Polynomial exists'',<ref name="julian4">{{cite journal |last1=Sahasrabudhe |first1=Julian |last2=Ballister |first2=Paul |last3=Morris |first3=Robert |last4=Tiba |first4=Marius |last5=Bollobás |first5=Béla |year=2020 |title=Flat Littlewood Polynomial exists |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=192 |issue=3 |pages=977–1004 |arxiv=1907.09464 }}</ref> which he co-authored with Paul Ballister,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Paul Balister |url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/people/paul.balister |access-date=2024-03-11 |website=www.maths.ox.ac.uk}}</ref> [[Béla Bollobás|Bela Bollobás]], [[Robert Morris (mathematician)|Robert Morris]], and Marius Tiba.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marius Tiba |url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/people/marius.tiba |access-date=2024-03-11 |website=www.maths.ox.ac.uk}}</ref> This work confirms the Littlewood conjecture by demonstrating the existence of Littlewood polynomials with coefficients of <math> \pm 1</math> that are flat, meaning their magnitudes remain bounded within a specific range on the complex unit circle. This achievement not only validates a hypothesis made by Littlewood in 1966 but also contributes significantly to the field of mathematics, particularly in combinatorics and polynomial analysis.

In 2022, the authors worked on [[Covering system|Erdős covering systems]] with the paper ''On the Erdős Covering Problem: The Density of the Uncovered Set''.<ref name="julian3">{{cite journal |last1=Sahasrabudhe |first1=Julian |last2=Ballister |first2=Paul |last3=Morris |first3=Robert |last4=Tiba |first4=Marius |last5=Bollobás |first5=Béla |year=2022 |title=On the Erdős Covering Problem: the density of the uncovered set |journal=Invent. Math. |volume=228 |issue=1 |pages=377–414 |doi=10.1007/s00222-021-01087-5 |arxiv=1811.03547 |bibcode=2022InMat.228..377B }}</ref> They confirmed and provided a stronger proof of a conjecture proposed by Micheal Filaseta,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael Filaseta - Department of Mathematics {{!}} University of South Carolina |url=https://sc.edu/study/colleges_schools/artsandsciences/mathematics/our_people/directory/filaseta_michael.php |access-date=2024-03-26 |website=sc.edu}}</ref> [[Kevin Ford (mathematician)|Kevin Ford]], [[Sergei Konyagin]], [[Carl Pomerance]], and Gang Yu,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gang Yu {{!}} Kent State University |url=https://www.kent.edu/math/gang-yu |access-date=2024-03-26 |website=www.kent.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref name="julian3" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Filaseta |first1=Michael |last2=Ford |first2=Kevin |last3=Konyagin |first3=Sergei |last4=Pomerance |first4=Carl |last5=Yu |first5=Gang |date=2006 |title=Sieving by large integers and covering systems of congruences |journal=J. Amer. Math. Soc. |volume=20 |issue=2007 |pages=495–517|doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-06-00549-2 |arxiv=math/0507374 }}</ref> which states that for distinct moduli within the interval <math> [n, Cn] </math>, the density of uncovered integers is bounded below by a constant. Furthermore, the authors establish a condition on the moduli that provides an optimal lower bound for the density of the uncovered set.<ref name="julian3" />

== Awards and honours ==
In August 2021, Julian Sahasrabudhe was awarded the [[European Prize in Combinatorics]]<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=2021 European Prize in Combinatorics - Dr Julian Sahasrabudhe {{!}} Peterhouse |url=https://www.pet.cam.ac.uk/news/2021-european-prize-combinatorics-dr-julian-sahasrabudhe |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=www.pet.cam.ac.uk}}</ref> for his contribution to applying combinatorial methods to problems in [[harmonic analysis]], [[Arithmetic combinatorics|combinatorial number theory]], [[Ramsey theory]], and [[probability theory]].<ref name=":0" /> In particular, Sahasrabudhe proved theorems on the Littlewood problems, on geometry of polynomials (Pemantle's conjecture), and on problems of Erdős, Schinzel, and Selfridge.

In October 2023, Julian Sahasrabudhe was awarded with the [[Salem Prize]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-28 |title=Salem Prize - School of Mathematics {{!}} Institute for Advanced Study |url=https://www.ias.edu/math/activities/salem-prize |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=www.ias.edu |language=en}}</ref> for his contribution to [[harmonic analysis]], [[probability theory]], and [[combinatorics]]. More specifically, Sahasrabudhe improved the bound on the singularity probability of random symmetric matrices and obtained a new upper bound for diagonal [[Ramsey numbers]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />

Sahasrabudhe is a 2024 recipient of the [[Whitehead Prize]], given "for his outstanding contributions to Ramsey theory, his solutions to famous problems in complex analysis and random matrix theory, and his remarkable progress on sphere packings".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news/2024-lms-prize-winners|title=2024 LMS Prize Winners|publisher=London Mathematical Society|year=2024|access-date=2024-06-28}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Sahasrabudhe's parents are television producers Deepak Sahasrabudhe and Susan Miller.<ref name="e026">{{cite web | title=About SOMA | website=somatv.ca | url=https://somatv.ca/about }}</ref><ref name="u013">{{cite web | title=Remembering the life of Sulabha Sahasrabudhe | website=Ottawa Citizen | date=2017-07-20 | url=https://ottawacitizen.remembering.ca/obituary/sulabha-sahasrabudhe-1066389726/?proxy=original }}</ref> His grandfather, Madhu Sahasrabudhe, was the acting director of the Food Research Institute of [[Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada]].<ref name="j238">{{cite web | title=SAHASRABUDHE Obituary (2004) | website=Legacy.com | date=2004-08-02 | url=https://www.legacy.com/ca/obituaries/theglobeandmail/name/-sahasrabudhe-obituary?id=41774096 }}</ref>
